A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMT research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original CMT and baseline experiments on four molecular systems, including quantitative results and constraint ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports revised molecular sampling results and additional original schedule, sensitivity, distribution-quality, and molecular-dynamics comparisons.

M1.justification: The constrained objectives, normalizing-flow architecture, importance-weighted forward-KL loss, and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedure. The chosen annealing-step notation clarifies an existing fixed budget; the newly tested variants are ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate alanine dipeptide, tetrapeptide, hexapeptide, and ELIL tetrapeptide at 300 K. Regenerated reference samples, additional metrics, and budget comparisons retain the same molecular populations and sampling task.

E2.justification: The principal baselines remain FAB, TA-BG, forward KL, and reverse KL. Appendix B adds a constant-multiplier comparator and a direct CMT-versus-MD comparison. The retained Ram-T-W2 comparison moves from Table 2 to Table 4 without the forward- and reverse-KL rows.

E3.justification: v2 regenerates the MD reference datasets; ELIL changes from a 2 fs timestep and 1 microsecond production to 1 fs and 2 microseconds. TA-BG budgets increase, including ELIL annealed training from 600,000 to 1,350,000 updates. Ram TV gains bin-area weighting, and new TICA, energy-Wasserstein, and MD free-energy-error evaluation protocols are introduced.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained constraint ablations, v2 tests adaptive versus constant multipliers, longer TA-BG schedules, entropy-bound sensitivity, and annealing-parameter trajectories. Energy histograms and TICA comparisons at different sample sizes add diagnostics of distribution quality and metric reliability (Appendix B and Figure 12).

E5.justification: v1 reports four independent runs for all main comparisons. v2 explicitly states that ELIL TA-BG results use only two successful runs because of numerical instability. Mean-and-standard-error reporting otherwise remains unchanged; this revises the reported replicate basis.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 replace many results under revised evaluation settings. For example, ELIL ESS changes from 26.18%/10.14% for CMT/TA-BG to 26.06%/13.75%; these are not same-setting performance gains. The ELIL Ram TV winner changes from CMT to TA-BG. New results include TICA and energy comparisons, dual-optimization timings, and approximately tenfold lower target-evaluation requirements for CMT versus MD in Figure 11.

T1.justification: The main propositions, Theorem 2.4, Appendix A proofs, and Appendix C.3 derivation remain unchanged. Section D.3.2 revises the Ram TV definition by adding bin area a_ij = (2π/100)^2. The new C.5 path formula also reverses the beta exponents relative to retained Equation (12), introducing an inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the dual-constraint framework, energy-only learning, ELIL benchmark contribution, and claimed greater-than-2.5-fold ESS advantage. New supporting analyses do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 identifies the large gradient-update requirement as a limitation and explains why analytical beta trajectories do not reliably measure the fitted model's closeness to the target (Figure 12). It expands the discussion of small-sample Wasserstein/TICA limitations and computational tradeoffs while retaining the original interpretation of the constraints.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-code and MD-data access information, fuller instructions for generating reference datasets, and dual-optimization timings. Table 11 explicitly lists previously implied CMT annealing-step counts. Conversely, C.4 removes the explicit search procedure and the disclosure of approximately 4–8 hyperparameter-tuning runs per system.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on mode collapse and mass teleportation, explicitly distinguishing its terminology from Máté and Fleuret's usage. It removes several citations, including Havens, Nam, Plainer, and Guo; the first trust-region/annealing connection is now attributed only to Blessing et al. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The main section order and Appendices A–D remain intact, with most original prose retained. Localized edits affect the introduction, related work, conclusion, and hyperparameter guidance; affiliations are expanded, and a reproducibility statement and Appendix C.5 are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn using stacked density paths. Six analysis figures are added as Figures 7–12, alongside new Wasserstein/TICA, timing, and annealing-step tables. Existing Wasserstein material is reorganized from Table 2 into Table 4, while v1's Figure 7 is retained as Figure 13.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evaluation weaknesses through corrected Ram TV normalization, regenerated MD references addressing reported bias, and better-matched TA-BG training budgets. Added diagnostics and code/data access information substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh remaining inconsistencies: the retained all-metrics superiority claim conflicts with TA-BG's better ELIL Ram TV in Table 1, and the new C.5 formula reverses the annealing exponents.
